**STEP 1 - Scene:** A small side dish of cooked, wilted green vegetables (looks like bok choy or similar Asian greens, stems and leaves), photographed from above at a near-top-down angle on a white square plate.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white square plate is roughly 22 cm across its width. Area ≈ 22 × 22 × 0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm²; I'll use ~400 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Cooked bok choy (white stems and dark green leaves). No visible oil or sauce pooling.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The greens cover roughly 20% of the plate area, about 80 cm².

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Pile height is about 2.5 cm on average, so 80 cm² × 2.5 cm ≈ 200 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cooked cut greens with a mix of stems and leaves, density ~0.2 g/ml → about 40 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked bok choy ≈ 13 kcal/100 g. 40 g × 13 kcal/100 g ≈ 5 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A small pile covering about a fifth of a plate, with no oil or dressing visible, plausibly weighs 30–50 g and provides only a few tens of kcal at most. About 40 g and 5 kcal is consistent with a light side of cooked greens. Note that cooked greens are very low in energy, so the figure is small even if the weight is off by a factor of two.
